walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: The engine of ADR 0046. Tree-sitter reads TypeScript and TSX through one query file: definitions qualified by what holds them, with TypeScript's visibility and whether code outside the file reaches them; references with their evidence kind, call or import, and type-only; imports resolved on each pass through the nearest tsconfig.json, its paths and the @/ alias; and the names of environment values and events written as strings. Code that did not parse holds no facts. Every other file is read as text. It finds where a symbol a file names is defined, through an import and every re-export. One cache entry per file, keyed on the hash of its bytes and the grammar; a pass yields to the event loop after each parse.

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: The code pass of ADR 0046. It lists the files Git does not ignore in each registered checkout, resolves every anchor and binding through the code opener's checkout rules, and asks code facts for each file: a bound symbol must be a definition, and an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH for an anchor whose symbol is defined outside the bound code of both ends or whose uses are of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. From the code facts of every bound file it reads the evidence between the bound parts of each board, owned by the narrowest binding: a use at run time reached through an import is a call, a use only as a type an import. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part that code reaches with no relationship, RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged against the evidence kinds that the vault configuration lets its kind accept. For each container bound to a module, a directory or its index file, it holds the interface that ADR 0044 derives against what the module exposes, as code facts read it: ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED for an entry point that owns nothing the module exposes while a drawn caller's code reaches it from outside the module, CALLER_UNDRAWN for a hidden part whose exposed code a file outside the module uses at run time where no part on the board owns that use, and EXPOSED_UNUSED, information, for exposed names no file outside the module uses. A module it cannot read is skipped as exposure-unknown. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped with the reason, a symbol found only in code that did not parse and a missing or failed language server among them.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: The engine of ADR 0046. A table of adapters names, for each language a grammar reads, its file extensions with their tree-sitter grammar, its query file, the function that turns captures into facts and the resolver of its imports; a new language adds its own files and one entry. TypeScript and TSX: definitions qualified by what holds them, with TypeScript visibility; imports resolved through the nearest tsconfig.json, its paths and the @/ alias. Python: module-level names and class members, exposed when __all__ lists them or, with no __all__, when they do not start with _; imports absolute, relative and of a package, a name resolving to its submodule where one exists, against the importing file own root, the source roots of pyproject.toml or setup.cfg, and src. Every adapter gives references with their evidence kind, call or import, and type-only, and the names of environment values and events written as strings. Code that did not parse holds no facts. Every other file is read as text. It finds where a symbol a file names is defined, through an import and every re-export. Each language adapter says what a module exposes: for TypeScript, the names its root files export, or the files its package.json exports names. One cache entry per file, keyed on the hash of its bytes and the grammar; grammars load on first use, and a pass yields to the event loop after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per checkout on its first question, speaks JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing over the child's stdio, and asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use's spelling on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. Every server it started has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill after a bound, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. The command of each language comes from language-servers.json in the state directory; TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp --stdio of Archboard's own typescript package, never the TypeScript of a checkout. A server that is missing or fails is said once, and its questions stay unanswered.

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: The code pass of ADR 0046. It lists the files Git does not ignore in each registered checkout, resolves every anchor and binding through the code opener's checkout rules, and asks code facts for each file: a bound symbol must be a definition, and an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH for an anchor whose symbol is defined outside the bound code of both ends or whose uses are of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. From the code facts of every bound file it reads the evidence between the bound parts of each board, owned by the narrowest binding: a use at run time reached through an import is a call, a use only as a type an import. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part that code reaches with no relationship, RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged against the evidence kinds that the vault configuration lets its kind accept. A module it cannot read is skipped as exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped with the reason, such as a symbol found only in code that did not parse.

nodes.name: Code facts

nodes.description: The engine of ADR 0046. A table of adapters names, for each language or format, the files it reads, how (a tree-sitter grammar and query, or a parser Bun has) and the resolver of its imports; a new language adds its files and one entry. TypeScript and TSX: definitions qualified by what holds them, with TypeScript visibility; imports resolved through the nearest tsconfig.json, its paths and the @/ alias. Python: module-level names and class members, exposed by __all__ or else by no leading _; imports absolute, relative and of a package, resolved against the file's own root, the source roots of pyproject.toml or setup.cfg, and src. Every adapter gives references with their evidence kind (call or import in code, configured-path in infrastructure) and type-only, and the names of environment values and events written as strings. docker-compose: the files compose finds in a directory and env files, parsed with Bun.YAML; services, networks and volumes are definitions (services.web); depends_on, links, volumes_from, network_mode service:, networks, named volumes and environment values whose host is a service are configured paths, settled by merging the base and its override in compose order and following container_name, hostname and network aliases; an env file gives names only, never values. Code that did not parse holds no facts. Every other file is read as text. It finds where a symbol a file names is defined, through an import and every re-export. Each language adapter says what a module exposes: for TypeScript, the names its root files export, or the files its package.json exports names. beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass. It reads the files Git does not ignore in each registered checkout through the code opener's checkout rules, asking code facts for each: a bound symbol must be a definition, and an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH for an anchor whose symbol is defined outside the bound code of both ends or whose uses are of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. From the code facts of every bound file it reads the evidence between the bound parts of each board, owned by the narrowest binding, a C or C++ file's part owning its pair where no part binds it: a use at run time reached through an import or an include is a call, a use only as a type an import. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part that code reaches with no relationship, RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged by the evidence kinds the vault configuration lets its kind accept. For each container bound to a module, a directory or its index file, it holds the interface that ADR 0044 derives against what the module exposes, as code facts read it: ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED for an entry point that owns nothing the module exposes while a drawn caller's code reaches it from outside the module, CALLER_UNDRAWN for a hidden part whose exposed code a file outside the module uses at run time where no part on the board owns that use, and EXPOSED_UNUSED, information, for exposed names no file outside the module uses. A module it cannot read is skipped as exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine: a table of adapters, each naming its files, how it reads them (tree-sitter or a Bun parser) and its import resolver. TypeScript and TSX: names qualified by what holds them; imports through the nearest tsconfig.json and the @/ alias. Python: module names and class members, exposed by __all__ or a name without _; absolute, relative and package imports against the file's root, pyproject.toml or setup.cfg source roots, and src. docker-compose (Bun.YAML): services, networks and volumes are definitions (services.web); depends_on, links, networks, shared volumes and environment values naming a service are configured paths, overrides merged in order; an env file gives names, never values. Nix: flake.nix read statically; each output is a definition by attribute path (packages.x86_64-linux.archboard), * for each system of an unread list; names below what it cannot follow are unknown, not missing; each flake.lock input is a build dependency. C and C++: names qualified with ::, with C's visibility; an #include puts its header's names in scope, resolved through compile_commands.json or relative paths; a header and its source are a pair. Swift: access levels; names resolve across a module and its imports; Package.swift, read statically, gives modules and build dependencies. C#: names by namespace, with accessibility and InternalsVisibleTo, resolved across a project and its ProjectReferences (build dependencies). References carry their evidence kind; environment and event names in strings count. Unparsed code holds no facts; other files are text. It finds a symbol's definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file, by its bytes' hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is

nodes.name: Code check

nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass. It reads the files Git does not ignore in each registered checkout through the code opener's checkout rules, asking code facts for each: a bound symbol must be a definition, and an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH for an anchor whose symbol is defined outside the bound code of both ends or whose uses are of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. A module it cannot read is skipped as exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped and why, such as a symbol found only in code that did not parse.

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine: a table of adapters, each naming its files, how it reads them (tree-sitter or a Bun parser) and its import resolver. TypeScript and TSX: names qualified by what holds them; imports through the nearest tsconfig.json and the @/ alias. Python: module names and class members, exposed by __all__ or a name without _; absolute, relative and package imports against the file's root, pyproject.toml or setup.cfg source roots, and src. docker-compose (Bun.YAML): services, networks and volumes are definitions (services.web); depends_on, links, networks, shared volumes and environment values naming a service are configured paths, overrides merged in order; an env file gives names, never values. C and C++: names qualified with ::, with C's visibility; an #include puts its header's names in scope, resolved through compile_commands.json or relative paths; a header and its source are a pair. Swift: access levels; names resolve across a module and its imports; Package.swift, read statically, gives modules and build dependencies. C#: names by namespace, with accessibility and InternalsVisibleTo, resolved across a project and its ProjectReferences (build dependencies). References carry their evidence kind; environment and event names in strings count. Unparsed code holds no facts; other files are text. It finds a symbol's definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file, by its bytes' hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH (a symbol defined outside the bound code of both ends, or uses of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept) and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C or C++ file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part code reaches with no relationship, and RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED (which, across a network hop, names the side without evidence) as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged by the evidence kinds its kind accepts. For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes: ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED, CALLER_UNDRAWN, and EXPOSED_UNUSED as information; an unreadable module is exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped and why, such as a symbol only in code that did not parse.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file by content hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per checkout on its first question, speaks JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing over the child's stdio, and asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use's spelling on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. Every server it started has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill after a bound, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. The command of each language comes from language-servers.json in the state directory; TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp --stdio of Archboard's own typescript package, never the TypeScript of a checkout. A server that is missing or fails is said once, and its questions stay unanswered.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: The one process that serves the vault: its routes, the one write boundary and the panes; callers reach it through the routes and the socket it handles
nodes.description: The CLI and the browser reach the server over HTTP and one WebSocket per page, so the routes and the socket they request are its entry points. Its lib/ files are private: other modules import only src/server/archboard/index.ts. The board lease reaches it through the onBoardLockChanged subscription that Board announcements registers.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps each checkout's commits onto the parts whose bound files they changed; says how far a board is behind, which parts change most or together, and what a branch changed against its proposal

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling over a period on request as checkout work; keeps each answer in memory until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: reads the board and the proposal named, then asks the history lens for the parts a branch changed; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH (a symbol defined outside the bound code of both ends, or uses of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept) and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C or C++ file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part code reaches with no relationship, and RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED (which, across a network hop, names the side without evidence) as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged by the evidence kinds its kind accepts. For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes: ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED, CALLER_UNDRAWN, and as information EXPOSED_UNUSED and a Terraform module's VARIABLE_PASSED_THROUGH and MODULE_SHALLOW; an unreadable module is exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped and why, such as a symbol only in code that did not parse.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file by content hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per checkout on its first question, speaks JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing over the child's stdio, and asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use's spelling on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. Every server it started has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill after a bound, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. The command of each language comes from language-servers.json in the state directory; TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp --stdio of Archboard's own typescript package, never the TypeScript of a checkout. walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. nodes.name: Language servers

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

walkthroughs.name: How the backend serves a board

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped and why. The header of src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code and the task that added it, and skills/archboard/references/authoring.md says what each one asks of an author.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file by content hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13, TASK-367.14, TASK-367.16 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per project on its first question: the checkout, or for Swift the package that holds the file. It speaks JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing over the child's stdio, and asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use's spelling on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. A language's row in languages.ts says what its server needs beyond that: Python's pyright has each file opened before a question and, through workspace/configuration, is told the interpreter of the checkout's own .venv or venv when Git tracks no file in it; C#'s csharp-ls is told the solution Git lists nearest the root; Swift's sourcekit-lsp starts with backgroundIndexing false so it never builds, is asked workspace/synchronize once so its index is loaded, and has each file opened before a question. Every server it started has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill after a bound, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. The command of each language comes from language-servers.json in the state directory; TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp --stdio of Archboard's own typescript package, never the TypeScript of a checkout, Python runs pyright-langserver or basedpyright-langserver from the PATH, and C# and Swift run only from an entry there. A server that is missing or fails is said once, and so is a Swift package with no index or a C# checkout with no solution or project file, for which no server starts; their questions stay unanswered.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration. It lists what it skipped and why. The header of src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code and the task that added it, and skills/archboard/references/authoring.md says what each one asks of an author.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file by content hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13 to TASK-367.16 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per project on its first question: the checkout, for Swift the package that holds the file, for C, C++ and Objective-C the directory of its compile_commands.json. It speaks JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing over the child's stdio, asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use's spelling on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. A language's row in languages.ts says what its server needs beyond that: pyright has each file opened and, through workspace/configuration, the interpreter of the checkout's own .venv or venv when Git tracks no file in it; csharp-ls is told the solution Git lists nearest the root; sourcekit-lsp starts with backgroundIndexing false so it never builds, is asked workspace/synchronize once, and has each file opened; clangd has each file opened and reads a copy of the database, its commands split into arguments by Code facts, in a temporary directory of its own where its background index and module cache stay, with --enable-config=false and no --query-driver, and is asked only once that index has ended. Every server it started has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill after a bound, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled, and its own directory is removed. The command of each language comes from language-servers.json in the state directory; TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp --stdio of Archboard's own typescript package, Python runs pyright-langserver or basedpyright-langserver and C, C++ and Objective-C run clangd from the PATH, and C# and Swift run only from an entry there. A server that is missing or fails is said once, and so is a project it cannot answer about, for which no server starts: a Swift package with no index, a C# checkout with nothing to load, a C file with no compile_commands.json; their questions stay unanswered.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. One table of adapters, src/runtime/code-facts/lib/adapters.ts, says which files each language or format reads, by extension or file name, with its parser (a tree-sitter grammar or one Bun has) and its resolver; each adapter's own files say what it reads. A definition carries its qualified name and the visibility its language gives it. A reference carries its evidence kind: call, import, configured path or build dependency; the name of an environment value or an event in a string counts. A resolver leads a use to the file or address it reaches: through an import or an include, or through the names that a module, project or package declares. Each language's rule in module-exposure.ts says what a module exposes. Code that did not parse has no facts, and a name the reading cannot place there is unknown, never absent; a file no adapter reads is text. It finds a definition and a module's exposed names. One cache entry per file by content hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.

nodes.name: Language servers
nodes.responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
nodes.description: TASK-367.13 to TASK-367.16, TASK-433 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per project on its first question: the checkout, for Swift the package that holds the file, for C, C++ and Objective-C the directory of its compile_commands.json. It speaks JSON-RPC over the child's stdio, asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. A language's row in languages.ts says what its server needs beyond that: pyright is told the checkout's .venv or venv; csharp-ls the solution nearest the root; sourcekit-lsp starts with backgroundIndexing false, is asked workspace/synchronize once and has each file opened; clangd has each file opened, finds its compile_commands.json where it would, keeps its own index where an editor's clangd does, and is asked once that index has ended. The command comes from server-command.ts. Every language but TypeScript runs only what the agent in that repository set on the checkout's registration (repo language-server), with the environment of the Archboard server and nothing added; if none is configured, the pass says so once for the checkout and the language, naming the command that configures one. TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp of the checkout's own typescript package from version 7 on, with its native program, both inside the checkout, else Archboard's own. Every server has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill of its process group, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. A server that fails is said once for its checkout, and so is a project it cannot answer about, for which no server starts: a Swift package with no index, a C file with no compile_commands.json.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. The header of src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code and the task that added it, and skills/archboard/references/authoring.md says what each one asks of an author.

nodes.name: Code findings memory
